prompts.useCase: explain a concept with a diagram
prompts.prompt: Why is the sky blue?
How does a four-stroke engine work? Take me through it one stroke at a time.
Explain to a six-year-old why the moon changes shape.

prompts.useCase: a picture of something in space or on a map
prompts.prompt: Show me the planets in order from the sun, with their sizes.
Should I rent or buy a home? Show me how to think about it.
Compare a heat pump and a gas boiler at a glance.

prompts.useCase: a data story with an animated chart
prompts.prompt: Show me how the world's population grew from 1800 to today, as an animated chart.
Make a title card for a documentary called The Last Glacier.
Write me a short poem about the first snow, and perform it.
I just got laid off.
Prototype the animation for a Pay button: idle, pressed, loading, success.
Design a three-second logo sting for a coffee brand called Ember.
Make a ten-second clip announcing that our bakery now opens at 6 am.
Storyboard a fifteen-second ad for a bike shop in four shots.
Tell me a story as a scene.
Paint me a lighthouse in a storm.
Pixel art of a fox.
An animated pixel campfire.
What is the boiling point of water at the top of Everest?
How do I undo my last git commit but keep the changes?
Give me five tips for sleeping better.

prompts.useCase: the open invitation that v0 answered by talking about itself
prompts.prompt: Show me what you can do.
Show me a map of the Silk Road with the main cities in order from east to west.
Make a timeline of the Apollo programme from 1961 to 1972, with the main missions.
Draw a family tree: I have two parents, each of them has two parents, and I have one sister.
Give me a flowchart for deciding whether to take an umbrella today.
How do I make pancakes? Show me the steps.
Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational, one step at a time.
Show me the water cycle as a loop that keeps going.
Compare cats, dogs and rabbits as pets in a table: cost, space and noise.
Show me how bubble sort puts these five numbers in order: 5, 2, 4, 1, 3.
Explain the offside rule in football with a picture.
Make a counting game for a four-year-old, with apples.
Show a toggle switch going from off to on, with its label changing to match.

prompts.useCase: a title with a stated length
prompts.prompt: Give me a five-second opening title for a podcast called Night Shift.

cases.useCase: a conversation across a look and a window change
cases.why: A change of look or window must not throw away the warm brain or the cache (P0-1): turns 2 and 3 should be since, warm and cached.

turns.text: Tell me how a bicycle stays upright.
Now show me how it steers.
Sum it all up in one picture.

cases.useCase: a viewer who cuts the answer off
cases.why: Speaking mid-answer must stop the old answer, leave the process warm, and tell the next brief what was and was not seen.

turns.text: Tell me the story of the first powered flight, scene by scene.
Actually, just show me the plane.

cases.why: A tap arrives as the next turn; the brain continues from what it offered.

turns.text: Offer me three weekend trips and let me choose one.
What should I pack for it?

cases.useCase: look at what you drew; fix it
cases.why: Can the model repair its own diagram from the sight report and the picture of the stage? Judge score before and after.

turns.text: Draw a diagram of how a bill becomes a law, with every step labelled.

cases.useCase: look at what you drew; fix it
cases.why: The same loop on a chart whose numbers have to be drawn to scale.

turns.text: Draw a bar chart of the five largest countries by area, in millions of square kilometres, drawn to scale.
